newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco was yesterday suspended until 2000 after being found guilty of taking steroids. The International Amateur Athletic Federation overturned a decision by Athletics Australia to allow Capobianco to compete due to alleged flaws in the testing procedure of the Perth sprinter. Page 20.

A late goal by Dutch captain Stephen Veen secured the Netherlands' victory over the Australian men's hockey side in the opening match of the Golden Jubilee hockey tournament. The 3-2 victory came after Australia twice squandered their lead over the Olympc champions. Page 18.

Triple Olympic medallist Daniel Kowalski has been forced out of next month's world shortcourse championships in Sweden, due to a chronic shoulder complaint. Kowalski's withdrawal will mean he will be unable to defend his 400 metre and 1500 metre freestyl titles. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Cronulla Sharks 34-8 Superleague victory over the Auckland Warriors has been marred by a video refereeing controversy and two contentious tackles. Cronulla prop Danny Lee was awarded a try in the 68th minute after video footage showed Auckland skippe Matthew Ridge forced the ball down safely in his in-goal area, while three Warriors were involved in two first-half tackles where they appeared to illegally lift Shark attackers from the ground.

A racial slur by North Sydney rugby league player Chris Caruana has seen him fined and dropped for a match. The slur made against Aboriginal opponent, Newcastle's Owen Craigie, has led Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker to admit last ight that North Sydney has an image problem.

Australia last night defeated South Africa by two wickets to win the second cricket Test and take an unbeatable 2-0 lead in the three-Test series. A massive six by wicket keeper Ian Healy sealed victory for the Australians, after Mark Waugh played a senstional innings to put his side in control.
THE AGE

Australian golfing sensation Stuart Appleby is to be included automatically into the US Masters after his one shot victory in the $US1.5 million Honda Classic. He will join fellow Australians Robert Allenby, Steve Elkington and world No 1 Greg Norman. Pae B8.

Allegations have been made that the Collingwood Australian Football Club is paying the wages of the Collingwood Warriors soccer team in defiance of the AFL Commission. While the AFL is adamant its members have no direct financial involvement with soccer,sources close to the Warriors claim Collingwood is guaranteeing the players' wages. Page B10.

Olympic bronze medal cyclist Bradley McGee smashed the Australian 4000 metres pursuit record - twice. McGee was in fine form for the Australian cycling championships, following his gruelling Australian one-hour record on Saturday night - lapping his fina opponent, Nathan Clarke, in four minutes 24.22 seconds. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

Controversy still surrounds Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor's future despite his team's victory in last night's second cricket test against South Africa. The Australians tried to distance themselves from the controversy surrounding their out-of-fom captain yesterday, despite calls that a loss of the Test could be reason for Taylor to stand down. Page 71.

In Hong Kong's biggest racing scandal for a decade, anti-corruption investigators questioned two of Australia's biggest names in racing - trainer David Hayes and Melbourne Cup winning jockey Damien Oliver. Both Hayes and Oliver were released after havingbeen taken in for questioning after a race last Sunday, however 36 others were arrested. Page 70.

The Australian Football League last night handed down tough penalties to Carlton Australian Rules players Simon Beaumont and St Kilda defender David Sierakowski. Beaumont has been ruled out for three matches for kicking, while Sierakowski received a fourmatch suspension for striking Carlton forward Anthony Koutoufides. Page 68.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Canberra Raiders rugby league player Quentin Pongia is set to miss up to five weeks on a high tackle charge. The Raiders can ill-afford to lose another player, with a crippling injury toll and three straight premiership losses so far this season. Page 5.

The Golden Slipper Festival has been hit by a downturn in betting revenue in Saturday's AAMI Guineas meeting. New South Wales punters invested a massive A$2 million dollars less than the A$10.9 million returns of last year. Saturday's figures reflect a rowing pattern, with off-course betting on the first three days of the Golden Slipper Festival down. Page 58.

Wallaby forward John Welborn has begun his bid to regain his spot in the New South Wales rugby union side for the opening round of the Hahn Cup on Saturday. Welbourn was forced to return early from the Wallaby tour of Italy and the UK with neck and shoulder injuries. Page 59.
